picks.excerpt: ByteDance unveiled World Apart at ChinaJoy 2026, an RPG whose NPCs are meant to interpret context, react to player decisions and generate dialogue in real time instead of reading pre-written lines. The studio still hasn't confirmed the underlying stack, with reports pointing to NVIDIA ACE.
picks.rationale: A major publisher betting a whole RPG on runtime-generated NPC dialogue changes what narrative and systems designers have to spec next.

picks.excerpt: Shift Up CEO Kim Hyung Tae defended the AI-generated Stellar Blade: Blood Rain music video by arguing the AI only rendered designs his team had already crafted by hand. Players rejected the framing, treating the output as evidence that generative rendering degrades the studio's own art direction.
picks.rationale: The 'AI only rendered our own designs' defence failed in public — a direct warning about generative marketing assets carrying a studio's art direction.

picks.excerpt: Veteran game-AI researcher Luke Dicken (Zynga, Take-Two) argues generative AI's real value in games is adaptive player experience, not automating art and production away. He also warns that today's per-player inference costs are unsustainable and hidden behind corporate subsidies.
picks.rationale: A credible practitioner draws the line between AI that improves play and AI that just cuts headcount — plus the runtime-cost math teams keep skipping.

picks.excerpt: Aftermath compiled a running list of 50+ independent studios that have publicly committed to shipping without generative AI. Cited reasons include training-data theft, environmental cost, labor displacement and the erosion of human authorship as a craft signal.
picks.rationale: A concrete, growing roster showing 'no genAI' has become a stated production policy and a marketing signal indies actively use.
